# StackKit

> StackKit is an independent, hand-checked directory of 52 tools for writers growing a newsletter on Substack (free and paid subscribers). Each tool has its real URL, pricing checked on 2026-10-21, who it's best for, and a short honest verdict. Not affiliated with Substack Inc.

Monetization: labeled sponsored placements, paid fast-track review, and affiliate links for some tools. Verdicts are not for sale.

## Key pages
- [Directory](https://stackkit.ink/): searchable list of all tools
- [Best tools to grow your Substack in 2026](https://stackkit.ink/guides/best-tools-to-grow-your-substack-2026/): long-form guide with starter stacks by budget
- [Datawrapper vs Flourish for Substack: which chart tool actually embeds?](https://stackkit.ink/compare/datawrapper-vs-flourish-substack/): Pick Datawrapper if you want interactive charts inside your Substack posts: it's the only one of the two that Substack embeds natively, and its free plan is unlimited. Pick Flourish only if you need animated or scrollytelling visuals and are happy to link out to them from a static image.
- [About & disclosures](https://stackkit.ink/about/)
- [Feature your tool](https://stackkit.ink/feature/): sponsorship options
- [Raw data (JSON)](https://stackkit.ink/data/tools.json)

## Growth & Notes
Referral networks, recommendation swaps, signup embeds and Substack Notes tools that bring in new subscribers.
- [Narrareach](https://stackkit.ink/tools/narrareach/) (https://www.narrareach.com/): Turning long-form posts into Notes and cross-posting to LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Threads and Medium. Pricing: From $19.99/mo ($199/yr); higher tiers $39/mo and $89/mo (discounted yearly). Verdict: Good if distribution beyond Substack is your bottleneck. Hands Notes to Substack's native scheduler rather than posting from a stored session.
- [SparkLoop](https://stackkit.ink/tools/sparkloop/) (https://sparkloop.app/): Getting paid recommendations and buying cross-newsletter referrals. Pricing: Free to join the Partner Network and Upscribe recommendation widget (SparkLoop takes a share of paid-recommendation earnings). Paying other newsletters to recommend you is a separate paid program. Verdict: The best-known newsletter recommendation network. Earning from recommendations is low-risk; paying for referrals only makes sense once you know what a subscriber is worth to you.
- [StackSweller](https://stackkit.ink/tools/stacksweller/) (https://stacksweller.com/): A simple cloud queue for batch-scheduling Substack Notes. Pricing: Pro $39/mo, or $25/mo billed yearly ($250/yr). Verdict: Does one job (a Notes queue that runs with your laptop closed). Be aware it works by holding your Substack session, and Substack now schedules single Notes natively.
- [Supascribe](https://stackkit.ink/tools/supascribe/) (https://supascribe.com/): Writers with their own website who want on-brand Substack signup forms, popups and landing pages. Pricing: Free for your first 100 subscribers captured and 1,000 embed views; a paid Pro plan after that (usage add-ons beyond plan limits). Verdict: Fills a real gap: Substack's native embed is fixed-width and unstyled. Independent (not affiliated with Substack), and only useful if you drive traffic from a site you control.
- [WriteStack](https://stackkit.ink/tools/writestack/) (https://www.writestack.io/): Writers who live on Substack Notes and want batch scheduling, research and Notes-to-subscriber analytics. Pricing: Hobbyist $23.99/mo ($239.88/yr); Standard $32.99/mo ($299.88/yr); Enterprise $99.99/mo ($959.88/yr); 7-day free trial. Verdict: The most complete Substack-only Notes suite. Pricey for a beginner, and publishing runs through a Chromium browser extension acting in your logged-in session.

## Analytics
See which posts, Notes and channels actually turn readers into free and paid subscribers.
- [Bitly](https://stackkit.ink/tools/bitly/) (https://bitly.com/): Tracking clicks on links you share to social, podcasts and print. Pricing: Free (with ads); Core $10/mo (annual only); Growth $29/mo; Premium $199/mo (annual pricing). Verdict: Handy for knowing which channel sends readers. The free tier is limited; many writers can get by with UTM tags plus Google Analytics.
- [Byline OS](https://stackkit.ink/tools/byline-os/) (https://bylineos.com/): Paid-newsletter writers who want MRR, churn, cohort and revenue-per-post analytics. Pricing: Starter free (CSV import, 30-day retention); Growth $19/mo; Scale $49/mo. 14-day trial. Currently in private beta. Verdict: Promising revenue-first analytics built specifically for Substack. It is a beta product; live sync uses your Substack session cookie and undocumented internal APIs, so the CSV-upload mode is the safer start.
- [Google Analytics](https://stackkit.ink/tools/google-analytics/) (https://analytics.google.com/): Seeing where your Substack traffic comes from (Substack lets you add a GA measurement ID). Pricing: Free. Verdict: Free and worth connecting on day one for referral sources. Overkill for most writers beyond the acquisition reports.
- [Orbit](https://stackkit.ink/tools/orbit/) (https://seeyourorbit.com/): Writers growing through relationships who want to remember who they've talked to across Notes, comments and DMs. Pricing: $12/mo or $120/yr, included with a paid subscription to creator Rebecca Spitzer's Substack. No free plan or trial. Verdict: A thoughtful relationship tracker for Substack that never writes or replies for you, and it connects to Claude. It works through a Chrome extension running alongside your logged-in Substack session (DMs off by default), and there's no way to try it before paying.
- [Plausible](https://stackkit.ink/tools/plausible/) (https://plausible.io/): Privacy-friendly analytics for your own website or landing page. Pricing: From $9/mo (Starter, 10k monthly pageviews); Growth $14/mo; Business $19/mo. Free trial. Verdict: Excellent lightweight analytics, but you can't install it on a substack.com publication. Use it on a personal site that funnels readers to Substack.
- [StackStats](https://stackkit.ink/tools/stackstats/) (https://stackstats.app/): Writers who want churn risk, cohort retention, superfan and growth-source analysis from their own Substack exports. Pricing: 1-year license $39 (renew updates for $29/yr; the app keeps working if you don't); Lifetime $79 early-adopter price (listed down from $129). One-time payments, no subscription; 14-day refund. Verdict: Digs far deeper than Substack's dashboard and keeps your subscriber data on your own computer (Mac or Windows). It's a new one-developer app: installers aren't code-signed yet, and the optional Auto-Sync (beta) logs in to Substack for you, so manual CSV exports are the cautious route.
- [Subshack](https://stackkit.ink/tools/subshack/) (https://www.subshack.pro/): Finding out which Notes and posts actually bring subscribers, and auditing your profile. Pricing: Free (Subshack 1.0), including a no-signup public profile audit. Verdict: A free, measurement-first browser extension that never posts for you. New and small, so expect rough edges.

## Cross-posting & Social
Schedule and repurpose your writing for X, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky and Notes.
- [Buffer](https://stackkit.ink/tools/buffer/) (https://buffer.com/): Scheduling Notes alongside every other social channel from one calendar. Pricing: Free (up to 3 channels, 10 scheduled posts per channel at a time); Essentials $5/channel/mo billed yearly ($6 monthly); Team $10/channel/mo billed yearly. Verdict: Reliable and affordable, and its free plan includes Substack Notes scheduling. The best default if you post to several networks.
- [Hypefury](https://stackkit.ink/tools/hypefury/) (https://hypefury.com/): Automating evergreen reposts and growth on X. Pricing: From $6/mo (1 channel) to $19/mo (all channels); 7-day free trial. Verdict: Strong automation for X-heavy writers. Less relevant if X isn't where your readers are.
- [Repurpose.io](https://stackkit.ink/tools/repurpose-io/) (https://repurpose.io/): Automatically distributing video and podcast clips across platforms. Pricing: Starter $35/mo; Pro $79/mo; Agency $179/mo (cheaper yearly); 14-day free trial. Verdict: Saves real time if you make video or audio. Pure text writers don't need it.
- [Taplio](https://stackkit.ink/tools/taplio/) (https://taplio.com/): Writers growing a professional audience on LinkedIn. Pricing: Starter $39/mo; Growth $69/mo; Pro $199/mo; 7-day free trial. Verdict: Effective for LinkedIn but expensive. Only worth it if LinkedIn is a primary acquisition channel.
- [Typefully](https://stackkit.ink/tools/typefully/) (https://typefully.com/): X-first writers who also want to post to LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky and Substack Notes. Pricing: Free (10 posts/mo); Creator $99/yr; Business $20 per social set/mo. Verdict: A polished writing-first scheduler with Substack Notes support. The free plan is enough to test it.

## Design
Header images, social cards and brand visuals without hiring a designer.
- [Canva](https://stackkit.ink/tools/canva/) (https://www.canva.com/): Header images, social graphics, Notes images and simple brand kits. Pricing: Free; Pro US$144/yr for one person (before tax). Verdict: The default design tool for newsletter writers. The free plan covers most needs.
- [Figma](https://stackkit.ink/tools/figma/) (https://www.figma.com/): Custom visual systems, templates and detailed design work. Pricing: Free Starter; Professional full seat $16/mo. Verdict: More power than most writers need. Pick it if you already know it or want pixel-level control.
- [Kittl](https://stackkit.ink/tools/kittl/) (https://www.kittl.com/): Typography-heavy graphics and AI-assisted illustrations. Pricing: Free plan; paid Pro, Expert and Max plans (see pricing page). Verdict: A stylish Canva alternative with great type tools. The free plan is for personal use only.
- [remove.bg](https://stackkit.ink/tools/remove-bg/) (https://www.remove.bg/): One-click background removal for headshots and product images. Pricing: Free to try; paid plans for full-resolution output (see pricing page). Verdict: Fast and accurate. Now a Canva brand, and Canva Pro includes a background remover, so you may not need both.
- [Unsplash](https://stackkit.ink/tools/unsplash/) (https://unsplash.com/): Free, high-quality photos for post headers. Pricing: Free to use under the Unsplash License. Verdict: The go-to free photo library. Popular images show up everywhere, so crop or edit them to stand out.

## Editing & Proofreading
Catch typos, tighten sentences and keep your voice.
- [Grammarly](https://stackkit.ink/tools/grammarly/) (https://www.grammarly.com/): Catching typos and clarity issues everywhere you write, including the Substack editor. Pricing: Free; Pro from $12/mo. Verdict: The free browser extension is worth installing. Pro's rewrites can flatten your voice, so accept suggestions selectively.
- [Hemingway Editor](https://stackkit.ink/tools/hemingway-editor/) (https://hemingwayapp.com/): Making dense posts easier to read. Pricing: Free web editor; Editor Plus from $8.33/mo billed annually ($100/yr). Verdict: The free web version does the core job (highlighting long and passive sentences). Most writers don't need Plus.
- [LanguageTool](https://stackkit.ink/tools/languagetool/) (https://languagetool.org/): Multilingual writers and anyone who wants a Grammarly alternative. Pricing: Free; Premium $24.90/mo monthly or $69.90/yr. Verdict: Strong grammar checking across many languages, and much cheaper per year than monthly billing.
- [ProWritingAid](https://stackkit.ink/tools/prowritingaid/) (https://prowritingaid.com/): Deep style reports for long-form and fiction writers. Pricing: Free; Premium $10/mo billed yearly ($120) or $30/mo monthly. Verdict: More thorough reports than Grammarly. Worth trying if you write long essays or serialized fiction.
- [QuillBot](https://stackkit.ink/tools/quillbot/) (https://quillbot.com/): Paraphrasing, summarizing and quick rewrites. Pricing: Free; Premium $19.95/mo or $99.95/yr. Verdict: Useful for tightening a stubborn paragraph. Don't lean on it for whole posts, because readers subscribe for your voice.

## Planning, Research & Automation
Editorial calendars, idea capture, research and automations.
- [Google Trends](https://stackkit.ink/tools/google-trends/) (https://trends.google.com/): Checking whether a topic is rising before you write about it. Pricing: Free. Verdict: A quick, free sanity check for timely topics and post titles.
- [Notion](https://stackkit.ink/tools/notion/) (https://www.notion.com/): Editorial calendars, idea banks and sponsor CRMs. Pricing: Free; Plus $10/seat/mo. Verdict: The most flexible planning hub for newsletter writers. The free plan covers solo use.
- [Obsidian](https://stackkit.ink/tools/obsidian/) (https://obsidian.md/): Building a personal knowledge base of notes, quotes and ideas. Pricing: Free; optional Sync $4/mo and Publish $8/mo (billed annually). Verdict: Great for writers who think in linked notes. Your files stay local in Markdown.
- [Readwise](https://stackkit.ink/tools/readwise/) (https://readwise.io/): Collecting highlights from books and articles to feed your writing. Pricing: Readwise Full $9.99/mo billed annually ($12.99 monthly); Lite $5.59/mo billed annually. Verdict: A strong research engine for essayists and curators. Its Reader app is included with Full.
- [Trello](https://stackkit.ink/tools/trello/) (https://trello.com/): A simple kanban for drafts moving from idea to published. Pricing: Free (up to 10 collaborators); Standard $5/user/mo billed annually. Verdict: Simpler than Notion if you only need a board. Free is plenty for one writer.
- [Zapier](https://stackkit.ink/tools/zapier/) (https://zapier.com/): Automating busywork such as logging new posts to a spreadsheet or sending sponsor reminders. Pricing: Free; Professional from $19.99/mo. Verdict: Powerful glue between apps. Substack has no official public API, so automations usually start from its RSS feed or email.

## AI Writing & Research
AI assistants for brainstorming, outlining, critique and research. Use with care.
- [ChatGPT](https://stackkit.ink/tools/chatgpt/) (https://chatgpt.com/): Brainstorming angles, outlines, headlines and research summaries. Pricing: Free; Plus $20/mo. Verdict: A versatile thinking partner. Use it for ideas and edits rather than finished prose your readers will recognize as generic.
- [Claude](https://stackkit.ink/tools/claude/) (https://claude.ai/): Long-document feedback, structural edits and drafting help. Pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo or $17/mo billed annually. Verdict: Particularly good at critiquing long drafts. The same caution about voice applies.
- [Perplexity](https://stackkit.ink/tools/perplexity/) (https://www.perplexity.ai/): Quick research with cited sources. Pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo. Verdict: Faster than a search engine for background research. Always click through and verify the citations.
- [Sudowrite](https://stackkit.ink/tools/sudowrite/) (https://sudowrite.com/): Fiction writers publishing serialized stories. Pricing: Hobby & Student $10/mo; Professional $22/mo; Max $44/mo; free trial. Verdict: Purpose-built for fiction. Not the right tool for essays or news-style newsletters.

## Audio, Podcast & Video
Record, edit and repurpose audio and video for Substack podcasts and social clips.
- [Adobe Podcast](https://stackkit.ink/tools/adobe-podcast/) (https://podcast.adobe.com/): Making laptop-mic recordings sound clean (Enhance Speech). Pricing: Free tier; premium features require a paid Adobe plan (check site for current offer). Verdict: Enhance Speech is impressive on the free tier. Check Adobe's current plans before relying on premium features.
- [Audacity](https://stackkit.ink/tools/audacity/) (https://www.audacityteam.org/): Recording and cleaning up voiceovers on a zero budget. Pricing: Free and open source. Verdict: Dated interface but free and capable for simple narration edits.
- [Descript](https://stackkit.ink/tools/descript/) (https://www.descript.com/): Editing podcast and video by editing the transcript. Pricing: Free; Hobbyist $16/mo billed annually ($24 monthly); Creator $24/mo annually ($35 monthly). Verdict: The easiest way for writers to edit audio and video. A natural fit for Substack podcasts.
- [ElevenLabs](https://stackkit.ink/tools/elevenlabs/) (https://elevenlabs.io/): Producing audio versions of posts with natural-sounding AI voices. Pricing: Free (10k credits/mo); Starter $6/mo; Creator $22/mo; higher tiers available. Verdict: Best-in-class AI voice. Tell listeners when a voice is synthetic.
- [OpusClip](https://stackkit.ink/tools/opusclip/) (https://www.opus.pro/): Turning long videos or podcast episodes into short social clips. Pricing: Free (60 credits/mo); Starter $15/mo; Pro $14.50/mo billed annually. Verdict: Fast way to get shorts from long recordings. Review the AI's clip choices before posting.
- [Riverside](https://stackkit.ink/tools/riverside/) (https://riverside.com/): Recording remote interviews in high quality. Pricing: Free; Pro $24/mo billed annually ($288/yr). Verdict: Records each guest locally, so remote interviews sound studio-grade. Ideal for interview-driven newsletters.

## Embeds & Interactive
Forms, charts and link pages that add interactivity around your newsletter.
- [Datawrapper](https://stackkit.ink/tools/datawrapper/) (https://www.datawrapper.de/): Clean, accurate charts, maps and tables for data-driven posts. Pricing: Free (unlimited charts, maps and tables, with a "Created with Datawrapper" credit); Pro $21/user/mo excl. VAT (removes the credit); Business $39/user/mo excl. VAT. Verdict: Newsroom-quality charts for free, and the one chart tool Substack embeds natively: paste the chart's share link into your draft. Interactive on the web and in the app; static in the email version.
- [Flourish](https://stackkit.ink/tools/flourish/) (https://flourish.studio/): Animated and interactive charts and scrollytelling. Pricing: Free (public publishing with attribution); paid Presenter (via Canva Business) and Publisher/Enterprise plans on contract. Verdict: More dramatic visuals than Datawrapper, but Substack doesn't list Flourish among its supported embeds and pasted embed code doesn't work, so plan on a static image linked to the interactive version.
- [Linktree](https://stackkit.ink/tools/linktree/) (https://linktr.ee/): A link-in-bio page that points social followers to your Substack. Pricing: Free; Starter $6/mo billed annually ($8 monthly); Pro $12/mo billed annually ($15 monthly); Premium $30/mo billed annually ($35 monthly). Verdict: Fine for bios, but your Substack homepage can often serve as the link. Only pay if you need the analytics.
- [Tally](https://stackkit.ink/tools/tally/) (https://tally.so/): Reader surveys, sponsor inquiry forms and feedback forms. Pricing: Free (unlimited forms and submissions); Pro $24/mo; Business $74/mo. Verdict: The most generous free form builder. Substack posts can't host forms directly, so link to it from your post or About page.

## Sponsorships & Monetization
Sponsor marketplaces, digital product sales and tips beyond paid subscriptions.
- [Gumroad](https://stackkit.ink/tools/gumroad/) (https://gumroad.com/): Selling ebooks, templates and guides alongside your newsletter. Pricing: No monthly fee; 10% + $0.50 per transaction on direct sales (profile or direct links); 30% on sales through Gumroad Discover. Verdict: The simplest way to sell a digital product to your readers. Fees are high per sale but there's no fixed cost.
- [Hecto](https://stackkit.ink/tools/hecto/) (https://www.hecto.io/): Selling sponsorship slots with transparent, upfront prices. Pricing: Marketplace; creators list ad packages with upfront prices (platform pricing on its site). Verdict: A straightforward sponsorship marketplace. Listing is easy, but demand varies by niche.
- [Ko-fi](https://stackkit.ink/tools/ko-fi/) (https://ko-fi.com/): One-off tips from readers who won't commit to a paid subscription. Pricing: Free with a 5% platform fee on some features; Ko-fi Gold $12/mo for 0% platform fee. Verdict: A low-friction tip jar that complements paid subscriptions.
- [Paved](https://stackkit.ink/tools/paved/) (https://www.paved.com/): Established newsletters looking for sponsor demand. Pricing: Not publicly listed for publishers (advertiser budgets from under $1,000). Verdict: A large newsletter ad network. Advertisers want audience size and data, so it suits writers with a sizable list.
- [Swapstack](https://stackkit.ink/tools/swapstack/) (https://www.swapstack.co/): Finding sponsors and affiliate deals for small and mid-sized newsletters. Pricing: Pricing not listed on the homepage. Verdict: One of the original newsletter sponsorship marketplaces. Worth a free signup to see what deals match your niche.
